beats: Hook (line_qc_hier_endless_desk): your laptop never keeps all its data in registers; every quantum computer today does. Is that why they are so hard to scale? Cast for all of QC01 (the six parts cut from her first lecture, Q25-01): the physicist (older, bald with a fluffy fringe, bushy moustache, goggles pushed up, lab coat) and the student (lanky, a tuft of hair, round glasses, striped long-sleeved T-shirt, messenger bag); both invented. No lecturer figure anywhere and never her likeness: her voice and her slides carry her part.
A huge design space and no clear winner among technologies (back to line_qc_thousand_tech_fair, planned in QC01-01; clip Q24-05 43:57-44:56).

The classical answer, a memory hierarchy: registers, cache, RAM, disk; fast, small and costly down to slow, big and cheap, working together (tape p15; reuse line_cluster_pantry_cellar or line_gpu_memory_reach; clip 66:45-67:35).
Horizontal scaling: more of the same qubits, all registers (line_qc_hier_endless_desk again; tape p16).

Vertical scaling: superconducting qubits as registers (gates 10-100 ns), ions and atoms as disk (slow, scalable), photons as the interconnect (line_qc_hier_tube_building for the idea, line_qc_hier_hybrid_lab for a real lab; clip 69:18-70:09; check the gate times on p16).

Moving a qubit between technologies (a transducer) moves it, it does not copy it; the hard part is the different frequency regimes (line_qc_hier_baton_handoff; her answer 72:16-73:59, cut before 73:59, which is a funding call).

Three axes a compiler faces (tape Q25-03 p14): the encoding: qubits, qudits, continuous variables (line_qc_hier_three_switches; reuse line_switch_dimmer); the model of computation: gates, measurement-based, analog (line_qc_hier_three_workshops: build brick by brick, carve a ready-made block, let the water find its way).
Each technology a different trade-off (Q24-05 42:21-44:56): photons fly but hardly interact, manufactured qubits are tunable but unequal, atoms are identical (line_qc_hier_tradeoff_trio).

Her philosophy: classical system ideas give the direction; the abstractions and solutions are rebuilt (line_qc_hier_compass_trail; clip 74:54-75:20; tape p17). Skip her remark about a named startup (Q24-05 45:24-45:50).
Cover (line_qc_cover_01_06; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the student whizzes on a wheeled chair along an endless desk covered in open books, no shelves anywhere.
